content.comment_body: Hello, I have 4 [product_name] modules connected to a [product_name] base unit. When I power up, the first two modules show a green indicator, but the third and fourth modules blink red. Also, when I connect to my PC, I cannot see the inputs or outputs for the last two modules. I have checked that the communication slider is fully to the left and tried moving it several times as suggested in various forum posts. I also tried powering the third and fourth modules with a separate power supply before the base module, but it made no difference. Does anyone know what the blinking red LED means and how to resolve it? Thank you, [user_name]

If the RUN / STOP LED is solid red, it indicates that the expansion module cannot communicate with the adjacent module. Usually, this is caused by dirty contact slides. Move the communication slides back and forth a few times to address this, or use electrical contact spray on the contacts and then slide several times to improve the connection. If that doesn't resolve the issue, try swapping the expansion modules to identify the problematic one.
The LED is not solid red, it's blinking. If I leave the communication slider disconnected, the LED remains solid red rather than blinking. So it appears to be a different issue.
The manual only describes the solid red LED and does not mention blinking red. I cannot provide any further information. It may be best to submit a support request.
I think I will contact support since I also couldn't find any information about the blinking red LED. Thanks for your help! Regards, [user_name]

Answering three questions points toward the solution: 1) How many local inputs and outputs can the [product_name] base module address? It supports 24 inputs and 20 outputs; the base module itself provides 8 inputs and 4 outputs. 2) How many inputs and outputs are on each [product_name] module? Each has 8 inputs and 8 outputs. 3) How many [product_name] modules can the base unit address? Two expansion modules, giving you a total of 24 inputs and 20 outputs.

As previously mentioned, you have exceeded the limits of the [product_name] setup. The last two expansion modules blink because the base module supports a maximum of 24 digital inputs and 20 digital outputs. The maximum configuration is the base unit and two expansion modules, for example: 8 inputs (base unit) + 8 inputs + 8 inputs (expansion modules) = 24 inputs. To use more inputs or outputs, you would need an additional base module. Further details about system limits are available in the manual, which can be downloaded from: [url]

You can't use four [product_name] modules on a single [product_name] base unit since it's limited to 24 inputs and 20 outputs. With the base unit's 8 inputs and 4 outputs, adding two more expansion modules completes the usable I/O range. Remove the last two expansion modules to solve the issue. If your project needs more inputs and outputs, you will require another base module.

analysis.insight_summary: Users experienced a blinking red LED on the third and fourth expansion modules when connected to the [product_name] base unit, which led to missing input/output visibility in the software. The primary user experience issue is unclear feedback—specifically, the lack of documentation or hardware indicators explaining the blinking red LED. The root cause is that the base module can only support two expansion modules, and this limit isn’t clearly communicated during setup.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect diagnostic indicators that clearly identify errors, comprehensive documentation on LED status behaviors, and an intuitive way to understand module limits without trial and error.
